observation: Local AI video guides this year are NVIDIA-first: the LTX team's guide treats an NVIDIA GPU with CUDA as a hard requirement, MiniMax H3 guides tier quality by VRAM from RTX 2060 to RTX 5090, and Mac users write up their own workarounds and timings (5 s of video in about 8 minutes on an M4 Max). The question people without an NVIDIA card keep asking is 'will it run on MY machine, and how slowly?', and they only find out after a long install and a first render.
suggestion: Add `funkbox doctor --bench`: after the usual checks, render a short shader loop off-screen at 1080x1920 on whatever OpenGL backend doctor found (GPU or software), print frames per second, and estimate how long a 20-second vertical Short's frames would take on this machine. One command answers 'is my laptop enough?' before the user commits to anything.
would_enable: A tip or myth-vs-fact promo that shows `funkbox doctor --bench` on three machines (CPU-only, Intel iGPU, a GPU) with their measured frames per second, instead of one machine per post.
